result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A new supplier gets 30 unless you give a value, and renegotiating means updating the supplier with the new value. The full suite passes offline (609 tests, including the two new ones in `SupplierTest`). Nothing is committed.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` has a new `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL CHECK (payment_terms_days >= 0)` column. Negative values are rejected the same way ratings outside 1–5 are.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. The old five-argument constructor is kept and defaults to `STANDARD_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30`, so the existing call sites in tests and the demo compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms. All supplier listings and lookups read the column: by name, by country, by minimum rating, `findSupplierById`.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: one test follows the Swedish example (45 days, renegotiated to 14, checked in every listing), and one checks the 30-day default.

Decision for you: I also added the column to the other queries that build a `Supplier`: purchase suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, supplier performance, spending, and categories with a single supplier. Without that, those reports would silently show 30 days for every supplier. Say if you want those reverted to keep the change to the four listings you named.

Caution: `updateSupplier` writes all fields, so a caller who omits the terms (using the five-argument constructor) resets them to 30 days.
